question.text: Hariyali Foundation (forest-conservation NPO) received INR 3 lakh of anonymous donations during the year. Total donations for the year were INR 40 lakh. Under Section 115BBI, what is the tax liability on the anonymous donations?

answer.text: INR 90,000 — the entire INR 3 lakh is taxed at 30% flat
INR 0 — fully exempt because INR 3 lakh is within 5% of total donations
INR 30,000 — tax at 30% on INR 1 lakh (only the amount above 5% of total donations)
INR 60,000 — tax at 20% on the full anonymous donation amount

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115BBI of the Income Tax Act taxes anonymous donations received by a charitable NPO at a flat 30%, but only to the extent the anonymous donations exceed the HIGHER of (a) INR 1 lakh or (b) 5% of total donations. For Hariyali Foundation, 5% of INR 40 lakh = INR 2 lakh, which is higher than INR 1 lakh, so the threshold is INR 2 lakh. Taxable anonymous donations = INR 3 lakh − INR 2 lakh = INR 1 lakh. Tax = 30% × INR 1 lakh = INR 30,000. The Trap: Taxing the full INR 3 lakh ignores the threshold carve-out. Treating the entire amount as exempt misses the 115BBI trigger altogether. The 20% rate is fabricated; the statutory rate for anonymous donations is 30%. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook states that anonymous donations received by a charitable NPO are taxable at a flat rate of 30%, but the cited pages do not spell out the "higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations" threshold or the resulting INR 30,000 computation. That threshold framing is taken from Section 115BBC/115BBI of the Income Tax Act rather than from the workbook pages checked.
